items.summary: Application status and reliability: Admins can now see application crashes, hangs and errors, with historical trends and event details. Drive health and storage trends: Admins can monitor individual drives, available capacity, health thresholds and historical storage consumption. VPN detection: VPN connectivity information is now shown for physical endpoints. It includes the connection status and adapter details. Diagnostics page: The Diagnostics page has been rebuilt with additional system health information, database activity and endpoint lookup. Support data exports have also been expanded. Multilingual interface: Real-Time Insights is now available in English and Japanese, covering menus, charts, alerts, diagnostics and date and number formatting. Nerdio Manager can pass the admin's language preference to Real-Time Insights, alongside the existing theme integration. Learn more... REAL-TIME INSIGHTS What is the feature? New views in Real-Time Insights for application health, drive health and VPN connectivity, plus a rebuilt Diagnostics page. What does it do for me? Application Status lists the applications that crash, hang or produce errors, with 24-hour tiles, trends and event details. The Drives section shows each local drive's capacity, storage trend and health. A VPN column and a padlock icon show when a physical endpoint is connected through a VPN. How do I configure and use it? Go to Observability > Insights > Real-Time . Use the Application Status tab, the VPN column on the Endpoints tab, and the Drives section at the bottom of an endpoint page. To open Diagnostics, press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+D on the Real-Time page. The interface is available in English and Japanese. Further reading: Insights: Real-Time Insights: Real-Time diagnostics

items.title: Executive Insights:
items.summary: Return on investment calculation amended: ROI is now shown as one data point per month, based on the highest value observed that month, with up to 12 months of history. The most recent month is shown only once all of its cost and license data is available. Administrative savings in ROI: Executive Insights ROI now includes the administrative time saved by recommendations the customer has completed. Time saved is valued using an average Azure admin cost of $70 an hour. Learn more... EXECUTIVE INSIGHTS: MONTHLY ROI AND ADMINISTRATIVE SAVINGS What changed? The ROI chart shows one data point for each month, based on the highest value observed in that month, with up to 12 months of history. The most recent month appears only when all of its cost and license data is available. What does it do for me? ROI now includes the administrative time saved by the recommendations you have completed, valued at an average Azure administrator cost of $70 an hour. ROI figures may look different from earlier versions. Further reading: v8.3 Changes to Executive Insights: ROI Changes Insights: Executive

items.title: AVD Insights
items.summary: Azure Capacity Extender metrics: Nerdio Manager now shows how often Azure Capacity Extender is triggered, over a selectable time range. Admins can use the counts to see how much value the feature is providing in their environment.

items.title: Windows 365 Insights now shows subnet IP usage:
items.summary: Windows 365 Insights now shows, and can alert on, subnet IP usage for Windows 365 endpoints, helping admins spot when there are not enough IPs to provision Cloud PCs. The tooltip for subnet IP usage on the Health page now states that it covers AVD, Windows 365 and Intune endpoints.

items.title: Cost groups with Entra groups:
items.summary: Admins can now add an Entra group to a User Cost Attribution (UCA) cost group instead of adding users individually. Nerdio Manager processes the group and passes its list of users to UCA.

items.title: Health Insights alerting for Nerdio Manager components:
items.summary: Admins can receive email or webhook notifications when a Nerdio Manager component's health changes to warning or unhealthy. This removes the need to rely on external tooling to be told about issues such as compute quota, VM SKU limits or database usage.

items.title: Nerdio Manager Copilot:
items.summary: Scripted Actions natural language creation: Admins can describe a Scripted Action in plain English using Nerdio Manager Copilot to generate the PowerShell script. The script is shown for review and editing before it is saved. This lowers the barrier for administrators without PowerShell scripting expertise. Copilot resource name customization: Admins can now customize the names of the resources used by Nerdio Manager Copilot. Unified Nerdio Manager Copilot and Azure AI settings: The Nerdio Manager Copilot and Azure AI settings sections are merged so all AI services are configured in one place. Azure AI features can use Foundry resources, and Copilot can use an existing Foundry resource without a separate deployment.

items.title: Reports [Private Preview]
items.summary: Windows 365 sessions: The reports page now includes data from all Windows 365 sessions. This data can be queried along with AVD session information.

items.title: Modeler updates
items.summary: Support for Mexico Central and Chile Central: The Cost Modeler now supports the Mexico Central and Chile Central Azure regions.

items.title: Intune Insights:
items.summary: Dashboard widgets unable to be modified: Resolved an issue where dashboard widgets could not be dragged or resized within Nerdio Manager. Mobile reports displaying on non-mobile devices: Resolved an issue where mobile reports displayed non-mobile devices. Tenant selector issue in Trends: Resolved an issue where the tenant selector in Trends did not resize correctly. Scheduled automations failing: Resolved an issue that caused scheduled automation processing to fail.

items.title: Terminal Services counters not collected:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the data collection rule created by Nerdio for Azure Monitor did not collect the Active Sessions, Inactive Sessions and Total Sessions counters because of an incorrect xPath filter. The filter no longer uses a wildcard, so these counters are now collected.

items.title: Missing "query" wording in Reporting:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where Reporting text still used the old "query" naming. The text now refers to reports.

items.title: UCA Entra group sync warning:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where User Cost Attribution (UCA) ran the Entra group membership sync even when no cost group used Entra groups, showing a warning on the UCA dashboard if the app registration had no Microsoft Graph group permissions.

items.title: FSLogix profiles missing from User Profiles:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the Collect FSLogix profiles information task completed only partially when profile files used an uppercase extension such as .VHDX , so some profiles did not appear in the User Profiles page. These profiles are now collected and listed, and the profile settings warning for the wrong-case extension has been corrected.

items.title: Remote Support [Private Preview]:
items.summary: Remote Support is a new way to provide remote assistance (attended or unattended) to your AVD session hosts, Windows 365 Cloud PCs, and Intune-managed Windows devices from Nerdio Manager. Unlike Console Connect (built on Zoho Assist), which relies on a third-party SaaS service, Remote Support is fully contained within Nerdio Manager. The Remote Support server and its supporting Azure services are hosted in your own Azure subscription. Admins can open a Toolbox session (terminal, file transfer, logs and power controls) or an Interactive user session (remote control) from the Connect dialog.

items.title: Nerdio Compass link in the header:
items.summary: A new Compass icon in the top navigation opens Nerdio Compass, which gives you a data-driven view of your legacy VDI environment to help you optimize, modernize and plan migration to AVD or Windows 365. The first time you sign in, a callout points to the icon. Close it once and it does not show again.

items.title: Simplified Settings navigation:
items.summary: The Environment page is removed from System > Settings. Azure, Nerdio and Integrations are now separate pages in the Settings menu instead of tabs, and breadcrumbs read, for example, System > Settings > Azure. Learn more... SIMPLIFIED SETTINGS NAVIGATION What changed? The Environment page is removed from System > Settings . Azure , Nerdio and Integrations are now separate pages in the Settings menu instead of tabs, and breadcrumbs read, for example, System > Settings > Azure. What does it do for me? Settings are one level closer, and the Knowledge Base articles show the new paths. If you cannot find a setting, search for it from the global search bar. Selecting a settings result takes you straight to that setting and highlights it.

items.title: Same-month Patch Tuesday adjustments:
items.summary: Schedules that use Days After Patch Tuesday can now be adjusted within the current month while the new run date is still ahead, so admins can delay patching by a day or two without recreating the schedule. If that month's cycle has already run, the schedule moves to the next month.

items.title: Task log scrolling enhancements:
items.summary: Job task logs now scroll to the latest activity automatically and keep your position when you scroll away. Keyboard scrolling with Page Up/Down and Ctrl+Home/End now works in logs and modals.

items.title: Resource Rules: VM family version v6 and v7:
items.summary: The VM family version selector in VM size rules now offers v6 and v7.

items.title: Language-based date and time formats:
items.summary: Dates and times in the Nerdio Manager interface now follow the format of the selected language, including date order, separators and 12 or 24-hour clock.

items.title: Custom domain for Web App resilience:
items.summary: The Web App resilience configuration now has an optional Custom domain name field, so you can serve Nerdio Manager from your own domain through Azure Front Door. After you run the generated script, create the DNS records it lists. The Front Door hostname keeps working alongside your domain.

items.title: Secure defaults for app registration:
items.summary: New installations now create the Nerdio Manager Entra app registration with implicit grant access tokens and ID tokens disabled, in line with security best practice.

items.title: DNS zone picker across subscriptions:
items.summary: The Microsoft Marketplace installer now lets admins select Private DNS zones from other subscriptions, supporting hub-and-spoke network designs with centrally managed DNS.

items.title: Private endpoint DNS record preview:
items.summary: When enabling private endpoints, Nerdio Manager Copilot, WinGet repository, Remote Support, Intune Insights, PII Detector, Real-Time Insights and User Cost Attribution now show the DNS records required before any resource is created, and skips creating records that already resolve correctly. Admins with centrally managed DNS can pre-create records, so Nerdio Manager does not need to change their DNS.

items.title: Host Pool modal tabs stay in view:
items.summary: On modals with a left tab list, including the Host Pool edit modal, the tab list now stays in view while the content panel scrolls independently.

items.title: Intune Insights signing key rotation:
items.summary: The Intune Insights JWT signing key is now rotated automatically every 90 days, with no admin action required. The interval can be adjusted between 1 and 365 days with the Features:IntuneInsights:JwtSigningKeyRotationIntervalDays app service setting.

items.title: Brazilian Real currency support:
items.summary: Brazilian Real is now available as a supported currency.

items.title: Consistent search bar placeholders:
items.summary: Search bars across Nerdio Manager now use consistent Search plus plural noun placeholder text, making it clearer what each search covers.

items.title: Notifications navigation and grouping:
items.summary: Announcements now appears above Cloud PC Alerts. The alert source label for AVD alerts reads AVD instead of Nerdio Manager. Conditions has AVD, Windows 365 and Intune groups, next to Health Alert Conditions. Actions are listed under Email and Webhook, an action with both appears in both, and an action with neither is listed separately with a warning. Active portal announcements also appear under Announcements.

items.title: Console Connect Toolbox setting:
items.summary: A Console Connect Toolbox toggle in Settings > Integrations > Console Connect > Common lets admins turn the Toolbox off, for organizations that require user consent before connecting. It is on by default and stays on for existing installs. When off, the Toolbox option in the Connect dialog is greyed out and Toolbox session requests are rejected.

items.title: Higher Console Connect license limit:
items.summary: Console Connect now supports up to 50,000 licenses per region, with your Nerdio entitlement continuing to set the effective limit.

items.title: Downloads for hardened storage accounts:
items.summary: Exported log files in task details can now be downloaded through Nerdio Manager when access to the storage account is restricted, alongside the existing pre-signed link option.

items.title: Export logs without sending:
items.summary: Admins can now export logs without sending them to Nerdio support. The Send button is now Export, and exported logs are available from the task details.

items.title: Log export download guidance:
items.summary: A tooltip now explains where to find exported logs when automatic sending to Nerdio support is turned off.

items.title: Migrate Enterprise Cloud PCs to Flex Dedicated:
items.summary: Nerdio Migrate now moves Windows 365 Enterprise Cloud PCs to Windows 365 Flex in Dedicated mode, reusing the source Cloud PC disk to preserve the user's profile, apps and OS state. Admins can migrate Cloud PCs in bulk batches with preflight validation and per-PC progress. Learn more... MIGRATE ENTERPRISE CLOUD PCS TO FLEX DEDICATED What is the feature? Nerdio Migrate can move Windows 365 Enterprise Cloud PCs to Windows 365 Flex in Dedicated mode, reusing the source Cloud PC's disk. What does it do for me? Users keep their profile, apps and OS state. You can migrate in bulk with preflight validation and per-PC progress. Microsoft limits the number of Cloud PCs under review (10 by default), and you can select up to 50 Cloud PCs in a batch. How do I configure and use it? Go to Cloud Desktops > Windows 365 > Enterprise , select the Cloud PCs, and then select Select bulk action > Migrate Enterprise to Flex Dedicated . You need a Flex service plan with enough spare licenses and a storage account in the same region as the source Cloud PCs. The migration deprovisions each source Cloud PC and unassigns its Enterprise license, so users lose access until the Flex Dedicated Cloud PC is provisioned. Further reading: Migrate from Windows 365 Enterprise to Windows 365 Flex Dedicated Nerdio Migrate overview

items.title: Under Review limit for Cloud PC migration:
items.summary: Cloud PC to AVD migrations respect the Windows 365 under review limit (default 10). The wizard shows how many Cloud PCs start immediately and that the rest wait for a free slot, and blocks the migration when no slot can free up, for example when the migration keeps the Cloud PCs under review. The selection cap is 50 Cloud PCs.

items.title: Scheduled snapshot deletion for Cloud PC migration:
items.summary: Cloud PC to AVD migrations can now delete the migration snapshot automatically after a scheduled delay, matching the other migration directions.

items.title: Improved Japanese localization:
items.summary: Improved Japanese translations across Nerdio Manager, including buttons, tabs, settings, tooltips, banners, error messages, search, Insights, Tasks, Notifications, Windows 365 and AVD Hybrid pages.

items.title: Resizable Policy Studio panes:
items.summary: Policy Studio panes can now be resized by dragging the divider, with minimum pane widths and a way to restore the default layout. The chosen split is remembered across navigation and sessions.

items.title: Libraries flagged by Defender for Cloud:
items.summary: Updated third-party libraries (AngleSharp, Microsoft.OpenApi, TinyMCE) flagged by Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

items.title: Key Vault API version update:
items.summary: Nerdio Manager now uses Azure Key Vault management API version 2026-02-01 or later, ahead of Azure's retirement of earlier versions on February 27, 2027.

items.title: Web App resilience script:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the Configure resilience script failed with “Login Failed” because Azure PowerShell was signed in to the wrong tenant. The script now checks the tenant before it continues.

items.title: Terraform module deployment:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the latest Terraform module failed to deploy when no local package path was set.

items.title: Session host provisioning with an Unknown egress path:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where session host provisioning failed at the Join to ARM AVD step when the host pool network used a subnet whose Egress Path is Unknown.

items.title: Private Endpoint page status:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the Private Endpoint page showed the wrong status for Public Access.

items.title: Updates page when Nerdio's update service is unavailable:
items.summary: The Updates page now shows a clearer message when Nerdio's update service cannot be reached.

items.title: UI fixes:
items.summary: Resolved several interface issues, including breadcrumbs after switching to the new menu, cut-off context menu options, a duplicated header on Custom View pages, missing RBAC filter values, and a job modal that could freeze.

items.title: Migrate fixes:
items.summary: Resolved several Nerdio Migrate issues, including license assignment and Cloud PC grace period errors and an interrupted migration failing at Import snapshot. Allotment fields in the AVD to Windows 365 Flex Dedicated wizard are now optional.

items.title: Security hardening:
items.summary: Strengthened access checks in Nerdio Manager.

items.title: Auto-scale hibernated VM usage tag:
items.summary: Powering on a hibernated VM with a disconnected session for administrative tasks no longer updates the NMW_LAST_USAGE_DATE tag. The tag is now updated only when a user signs in, so auto-scale decisions reflect actual usage.

items.title: Improved validation for group management:
items.summary: Added additional validation when Nerdio Manager needs to modify group membership.

items.title: Register Cloud Connectors with a registration code
Cloud Connector services on Microsoft .NET 10
Delete Azure Files auto-scale configuration:
items.summary: The auto-scale configuration for an Azure Files share can now be deleted, enabled, or disabled. This clears a disabled configuration that would otherwise remain indefinitely, and allows a configuration of a different generation (v1 or Provisioned v2) to be created for the same share.

items.title: Azure Files auto-scale 24-hour scale-in restriction:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the recurring storage auto-scale task repeatedly attempted to scale in an Azure Files share without honoring Azure's once-per-24-hours decrease restriction, generating failed scale-in tasks every cycle.

items.title: NetApp volume network features state:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where Azure NetApp Files volumes continued to display as using Basic network features in Nerdio Manager after being updated to Standard in Azure, affecting auto-scale for those volumes.

items.title: UAM deployment policy timeouts at scale:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where Application Deployment Policies targeting a large number of session hosts (more than 2,000) failed with a SQL execution timeout, preventing applications from deploying.

items.title: Intune Insights App Metering:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the collector remediation script could miss events on devices in time zones behind UTC. The script has been updated to collect all sources in all time zones.

items.title: Modeler pie charts missing from exported reports:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where pie charts did not render when a model report was exported, caused by an underlying library upgrade.

items.title: App Metering for Intune Insights (Public Preview):
items.summary: Track application usage across your Intune estate. This feature empowers administrators to discover and report on targeted application usage, which can help to inform software budgets or even identify and reclaim expensive un-used software licenses. Learn more... APP METERING FOR INTUNE INSIGHTS What is the feature? The App Metering feature within Intune Insights provides valuable metrics for app usage in your environment, and a potential route to significant cost savings, by allowing you to discover usage patterns in your environment on a per-user basis. What does it do for me? The insights gained from App Metering can help you to assess application criticality and to identify applications that are not used by specific users, which in turn allows you to reclaim and reuse expensive licenses. How do I configure and use it? Enable App Metering from Settings > Integrations > Intune Insights , then add and configure the applications you want to meter from Insights > Intune > App Metering . See Intune Insights: Enable and configure App Metering for full details. Further reading: Intune Insights: App Metering Intune Insights: Enable and configure App Metering

items.title: Nerdio Manager MCP support (Public Preview):
items.summary: Nerdio Manager now supports MCP read-only access from external AI agents. With this initial release, Azure Virtual Desktop information across the following areas are available via MCP: Workspaces, Host Pools, Host Pool Profiles, Desktop Images, Storage, and Logs. MCP can be enabled under System > Settings > Integrations . Note Equivalent AI functionality is also available natively in Nerdio Manager via Nerdio Copilot. Learn more... NERDIO MANAGER MCP CONNECTOR What is the feature? Nerdio Manager includes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) connector that lets you connect your preferred AI agent(s) to your environment. What does it do for me? Once connected, your AI agent can dynamically access real-time information about your environment's status across the following areas: Workspaces Host pools Host Pool Profiles Desktop images Storage Logs How do I configure and use it? Navigate to System > Settings > Integrations > Model Context Protocol to enable the feature, then follow the detailed instructions in Nerdio Manager MCP Connector to set up your AI client. For example, once connected you could ask your AI agent to "show me all my current host pools" or "write a PowerShell script to deploy the latest Windows 11 updates to my images." Further reading: Nerdio Manager MCP Connector

items.title: Microsoft Agent Updates:
items.summary: AVD Agent: v1.0.15294.200 FSLogix: 26.08

items.title: Unhealthy VMs unable to be deleted:
items.summary: Resolved an issue in some scenarios where deleting an unhealthy VM was not possible.

items.title: Host pool wizard missing hover details:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where hovering over desktop images or VM size SKUs would not function as expected.

items.title: Nutanix provisioning error:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where provisioning a Nutanix session host could fail when the Disable Local Admin setting was enabled within the Nerdio Manager settings.

items.title: Azure NetApp Files new volume error:
items.summary: Resolved an issue that prevented creating a new volume in an existing Azure NetApp Files account. Existing Active Directory connection settings are now preserved and used without attempting to reconfigure the account.

items.title: Cloud PC self-service context menu:
items.summary: No longer shown when no actions are available.

items.title: Server OS devices in Intune list:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where Windows Server OS devices enrolled via Microsoft Defender for Endpoint appeared in NME's Intune device list. These devices are now filtered out.

items.title: Intune policy status cache failures:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the Refresh Intune policy device statuses cache task failed repeatedly for some customers due to intermittent Microsoft Graph errors; the task now handles these errors gracefully without breaking its retry logic.

items.title: Cloud PC Alerts permission error:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where admins with a role below Windows 365 Administrator saw a raw Microsoft Graph 'Access is denied' error when viewing Cloud PC Alerts under Notifications > Windows 365. NME now shows a message stating the roles required to view alerts.

items.title: Throttling on All Devices page:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where opening Endpoints > All Devices timed out or was throttled for tenants with a very large number of Intune devices; admins can now enable the Features:IntuneCache:DisplayCachedDevices app setting to show cached device data instead of querying Microsoft Graph in real time.

items.title: App deployment preflight retries:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where Intune application deployment policy preflight checks failed with 'Too many retries' due to Microsoft Graph throttling on large tenants; NME now retrieves app installation status from an exportable report instead of a paginated one.

items.title: Nutanix on the Health page:
items.summary: The Health page now includes a Nutanix section, shown only where Nutanix is in use.

items.title: App Metering:
items.summary: In locales with time zones behind UTC (UTC-1 or earlier), the query that returns events to NME may occasionally miss events.

items.title: Reduced Graph permission for RTI/II SQL Managed Identity:
items.summary: The managed identity used by Real-Time Insights and Intune Insights SQL Server now requires the narrower Application.Read.All permission instead of Directory.Read.All.

items.title: Link additional Entra ID tenants via API:
items.summary: New API endpoints to add or remove a secondary Entra ID tenant by Tenant ID, matching the existing Settings > Azure Environment UI flow, with support for Azure Global, US Government, and China clouds.

items.title: Console Connect: higher default license cap:
items.summary: Raised from 5,000 to 15,000, removing a ceiling that affected larger deployments.

items.title: Console Connect: device-removal cooldown:
items.summary: Adds a cooldown period before a device is removed from Console Connect after an Azure API check, reducing unnecessary agent reinstalls.

items.title: Japanese localizations:
items.summary: Revamped and expanded various Japanese (ja-JP) localizations for improved accuracy and coverage.

items.title: SQL role migration script for Entra ID SQL authentication:
items.summary: Fixed a gap for customers on an older dbo-based SQL configuration. A new migration script automates moving database permissions to the recommended least-privileged roles instead of requiring manual reassignment.

items.title: Console Connect: device count instability after upgrade:
items.summary: Fixed an issue where device counts could drop sharply after an update, triggering unnecessary agent reinstalls.

items.title: Console Connect: bulk device removal:
items.summary: Fixed an issue where removing a large number of devices in one operation could fail; removals are now processed in smaller batches.

items.title: Device name template field removed from AVD to Windows 365 Enterprise migration:
items.summary: As flagged in the previous release notes, this field did not apply to the provisioned Cloud PC and has now been removed from the migration wizard. Migrated Cloud PCs retain the original AVD session host name. Root cause investigation is ongoing; the field will return once resolved.

items.title: Pre-created Entra ID app in advanced installations:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the scripted actions certificate (nmw-scripted-action-cert) was not uploaded to the app registration when you installed with a pre-created Entra ID application. The installation script now uploads the certificate automatically.

items.title: AVD Hybrid support for Nutanix AHV
items.summary: is now Generally Available.

items.title: AVD Hybrid support for VMware vSphere
items.summary: is available for Private Preview. To request access, please complete this form .

items.title: The following migration paths are now Generally Available: Citrix / Omnissa to AVD Personal Citrix / Omnissa to Windows 365 Enterprise
items.summary: The following migration paths are now Generally Available: Citrix / Omnissa to AVD Personal Citrix / Omnissa to Windows 365 Enterprise

items.title: Self-service portal now supports Windows 365:
items.summary: End users can now manage their own Windows 365 Cloud PC from the Nerdio self-service portal. When enabled by the administrator on a per-provisioning policy level, users with the End-user role and an assigned Cloud PC can Reprovision, Restore, and Restart it themselves, with Rename available to administrators. The Self-service portal page, if enabled, is now located at Cloud Desktops > Self-Service > Portal (moved from Cloud Desktops > Azure Virtual Desktop ). Learn more... NERDIO SELF-SERVICE PORTAL FOR WINDOWS 365 What is the feature? The Nerdio self-service portal now supports Windows 365, alongside its existing AVD personal host pool support. What does it do for me? End users with an assigned Cloud PC can reprovision, restore, and restart their own device themselves, without waiting on an administrator, if a policy administrator has enabled these for them. Rename remains an administrator-only action. How do I configure and use it? See the configuration guidance in Windows 365: Self-service portal . Further reading: Windows 365: Self-service portal

items.title: Host Pool Profiles
items.summary: Profiles Management has been renamed to  .

items.title: AVD Hybrid on Nutanix new features:
items.summary: Real-Time Insights: Nutanix host pools can now be selected and configured to use Real-Time Insights. Faster Nutanix session host deployment: The session host deployment process has been streamlined and optimized to reduce provisioning time and shorten overall host pool deployment times. Multi-selection enabled: You can now select multiple Nutanix host pools and session hosts on their respective pages to perform bulk actions. Session host location support: You may now choose the location when adding session hosts to a host pool.

items.title: Global Pools enhancements:
items.summary: Attribute assignment enhancements: When using the Attribute assignment mode for distribution, you can now select Entra ID attributes. The MemberOf dropdown now also supports selecting multiple Entra ID groups. Percentage-based distribution for assignment policies: Assignment policies within pool groups now support percentage-based distribution, allowing workloads to be distributed across pool groups according to configurable percentage allocations. Consolidated Global Pool policies: Assignment and failover policies for a Global Pool are now managed from a single Policies tab. Host pool bulk creation: Multiple host pools can now be created simultaneously within a pool group, streamlining large-scale deployments. Console Connect support: Global Pools can now be selected for Console Connect enablement. Real-Time Insights support: Global Pools can now be selected for Real-Time Insights data aggregation. Application policies support: Global Pools or their pool groups are now available as options for application deployment policies. Host pool profiles visibility: Global Pools and their associated pool groups are now visible on the Host Pool Profiles page. Learn more... GLOBAL POOLS ENHANCEMENTS What has changed? The Global Pools feature - released in v8.1 - gains several enhancements in 8.2: Entra ID attribute-based distribution now supports selecting attributes directly and multiple Entra ID groups in the MemberOf dropdown; assignment policies support percentage-based distribution across pool groups, in addition to the existing count-based method; assignment and failover policies are consolidated onto a single Policies tab; multiple host pools can be created simultaneously within a pool group; Global Pools can be enabled for Console Connect and Real-Time Insights; Global Pools and their pool groups are available as options in application deployment policies; and Global Pools are now visible on the Host Pool Profiles page. What does the change do for me? Together, these close several of the gaps between managing a Global Pool and managing a regular host pool: you can now apply the same UAM application policies, Real-Time Insights monitoring, and Console Connect remote support to Global Pools that you already use elsewhere, and distribute users across pool groups by percentage rather than only by count. How do I configure and use it? See the configuration guidance in Configure Global Pools . Further reading: Global Pools Overview Configure Global Pools UAM: Manage deployment policies (for the new application-policy support)

items.title: Host pool creation UI overhaul:
items.summary: Host pools are now created using a step-by-step wizard that guides you through basics, VM template, Active Directory, FSLogix, RDP, tags, and application policies with quick assign, replacing the previous single dialog pop-up workflow. Learn more... HOST POOL CREATION WIZARD What is the feature? Host pool creation now uses a step-by-step wizard - Basics, VM Template, Active Directory, FSLogix, RDP, Tags, and Application policies with quick assign - replacing the previous single dialog pop-up. What does it do for me? The same configuration is easier to work through, especially for less-frequent host pool creators, since each stage is presented on its own step rather than as one long form. How do I configure and use it? Navigate to Cloud Desktops > Azure Virtual Desktop > Workspaces . Select the desired workspace. Select New host pool . Follow the wizard's prompts to create a host pool with the desired settings.

items.title: Desktop image UI overhaul:
items.summary: The desktop image creation and set as image process has been reworked as a step-by-step wizard for a streamlined workflow. Learn more... DESKTOP IMAGES WIZARD What is the feature? Desktop image creation and the "set as image" process are reworked as a step-by-step wizard: VM, Join to AD, Settings, Clean up, Scripted Actions & Apps, Image, Replication, and Tags. What does it do for me? A more guided, staged flow for a process that previously required navigating one longer form. How do I configure and use it? Navigate to Cloud Desktops > Desktop Images . From the bottom-right of the page, select Create . Follow the wizard's prompts to create a desktop image with the desired settings. Further reading: Create a Desktop Image

items.title: Auto-scale for Azure Files v2:
items.summary: Auto-scale is now supported for Azure Files v2 storage accounts, with configurable thresholds and parameters for greater flexibility. Learn more... AUTO-SCALE SUPPORT FOR AZURE FILES v2 What is the feature? Auto-scale support extends to Azure Files v2 storage accounts, with configurable thresholds and parameters. What does it do for me? If you're using the newer Azure Files v2 storage account type, you get the same auto-scale cost/capacity management already available for other storage types. How do I configure and use it? See the configuration guidance in Auto-scale for Azure Files Storage Premium . Related: Auto-scale for Azure Files Storage Premium

items.title: Azure Files consent link opens in a new tab:
items.summary: The grant consent link shown when adding an Azure Files storage account now opens in a new browser tab instead of navigating away from Nerdio Manager.

items.title: FSLogix override profile path:
items.summary: For FSLogix host pool profiles, the Add profile assignments wizard now includes a Keep the override profile path option under the FSLogix profile selector, allowing the same FSLogix profile to be assigned to multiple host pools while retaining a custom profile path.

items.title: Application group name complexity support:
items.summary: We now support the ability to have spaces and periods within the names of application groups.

items.title: Migrate to a different virtual network:
items.summary: When migrating Citrix / Omnissa desktops to AVD, you now have the option to select a different destination virtual network and subnet, alongside a different resource group, subscription, or region, with a warning covering routing, DNS, and security control impact.

items.title: Host pools can now be cloned to another subscription:
items.summary: When cloning host pools, you may now choose Resource Groups in another subscription.

items.title: Desktop images with confidential support:
items.summary: Creating desktop images from Azure VMs now support inserting a third URL for when a Security metadata SAS URL is provided by Azure.

items.title: User interface:
items.summary: Improved the user experience and behavior when modifying FSLogix app service settings.

items.title: Revamped tooltips:
items.summary: Tooltips across the workspace and host pool pages for Azure Local and AVD Hybrid on Nutanix have been updated for improved clarity.

items.title: RDP Settings not being saved:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where editing custom RDP settings on a host pool did not save the new settings.

items.title: Application masking rules:
items.summary: The "Exclude local administrators" option now persists correctly when exporting and importing application masking rules across host pools.

items.title: Console Connect installation error on scheduled session host creation:
items.summary: Resolved an issue in some situations where the Console Connect agent would not install when session hosts are created on a schedule.

items.title: FSLogix profiles with special characters:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where resetting FSLogix profiles containing special characters would fail to locate the profile, most prevalent in Microsoft Entra ID hybrid joined scenarios.

items.title: AVD Hybrid on Nutanix Auto-scale cleanup:
items.summary: Enhancements have been made to the Auto-scale process to clean up resources that were created during the session host provisioning process if there was a failure.

items.title: Windows 365 menu restructure:
items.summary: The Windows 365 menu has been restructured into a dedicated page per provisioning type — Enterprise, Flex Dedicated, Flex Shared, and Cloud Apps — with provisioning policies and assignments shown on each page and filtered to that desktop type. Cloud PC alerts now appear only on the Alerts page.

items.title: User Experience Sync storage guidance:
items.summary: When configuring User Experience Sync on a Windows 365 Flex Shared provisioning policy, Nerdio Manager now calculates total pool capacity from the Cloud PC size and assignment counts already entered, showing a recommended per-user size and the number of profiles the pool supports. A non-blocking warning appears where the selected size may exceed available capacity. Learn more... STORAGE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR USER EXPERIENCE SYNC ON WINDOWS 365 FLEX SHARED What is the feature? When configuring User Experience Sync on a Windows 365 Flex Shared provisioning policy, Nerdio Manager now calculates total pool capacity from the Cloud PC size and the assignments already entered, showing a recommended per-user storage size and how many user profiles the pool can support. A related Cloud PC alert condition, Frontline Cloud PC User Experience Sync Storage Limits, reports when storage nears or exceeds its limit. What does it do for me? Removes the guesswork from sizing User Experience Sync storage for a shared-mode Cloud PC pool, and warns you before - and after - you run out of headroom. How do I configure and use it? See the configuration guidance in Use Nerdio Manager to configure and manage User Experience Sync for Windows 365 Flex in Shared mode . The related alert condition is configured like any other Cloud PC alert condition: see Alerts and notifications . Further reading: Use Nerdio Manager to configure and manage User Experience Sync for Windows 365 Flex in Shared mode Alerts and notifications

items.title: User Experience Sync storage limit alert:
items.summary: A new Cloud PC alert type reports when Windows 365 Flex User Experience Sync storage has reached or is approaching its limit. Severity, email recipients, and portal notifications are configurable, and occurrences are recorded in alert history.

items.title: Cloud PC removal and license unassignment:
items.summary: A new Remove host action on the Hosts page deletes a Cloud PC and removes the user from the provisioning group or groups assigned to its provisioning policy. For Enterprise Cloud PCs, licenses can optionally be unassigned at the same time, with any directly assigned licenses listed for manual removal. Direct license unassignment during Cloud PC removal requires the Microsoft license management RBAC permission (LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All): without it, the direct-license cleanup option stays disabled and the license remains assigned. Learn more... INTEGRATED REMOVE ACTION TO DELETE A CLOUD PC AND DE-PROVISION ITS ASSOCIATED LICENSES What is the feature? A Remove action on the Cloud PC hosts page deletes a Cloud PC and removes the user from its provisioning group(s), with the option to unassign the user's Cloud PC licenses - both group-assigned and directly assigned - at the same time. What does it do for me? One action now covers device removal and license cleanup together, rather than needing to do the license side separately (and potentially forgetting to, leaving a seat consumed unnecessarily). How do I configure and use it? From the Cloud PC hosts list, select Remove from a device's action menu. Choose which License cleanup options you want (each requires the Microsoft license management RBAC permission to enable). Type Confirm . Select OK . Further reading: Windows 365: Enable and configure Cloud PCs

items.title: Expanded AI-enabled statuses for Cloud PC hosts:
items.summary: The AI Status column now reports Ready To Use, Initiating, Failed, Disabled, and N/A, replacing the previous Enabled/Disabled states, for more precise visibility.

items.title: AVD agent removal during migration to Windows 365:
items.summary: Migrating an AVD session host to Windows 365 now removes the AVD agent from the source virtual machine as part of the cleanup step.

items.title: Cloud PC device name template:
items.summary: Provisioning policies now include an optional device name template, so Cloud PC naming conventions can be set in Nerdio Manager rather than in the Intune admin center. Templates are validated as they are entered and apply only to newly provisioned or reprovisioned Cloud PCs. Learn more... CLOUD PC DEVICE NAME TEMPLATE What is the feature? Provisioning policies now include an optional device name template field, so Cloud PC naming conventions can be set in Nerdio Manager rather than in the Intune admin center. What does it do for me? Keeps device naming configuration in one place if you already manage Windows 365 primarily through Nerdio Manager. How do I configure and use it? On the provisioning policy, enter a template such as CPC-%USERNAME:4%-%RAND:5% , using %USERNAME:X% for the first X characters of the username and %RAND:Y% (Y ≥ 5) as a required random suffix. The full name must be 4-15 characters, and the template applies only to newly provisioned or reprovisioned Cloud PCs. Further reading: Windows 365: Enable and configure Cloud PCs

items.title: Editable Cloud PC alert rule conditions:
items.summary: The conditions section of a Cloud PC alert rule can now be edited in Nerdio Manager, behaving as it does in the Intune portal. Changes apply to the Intune alert rule itself, so they affect every tool reading that rule. Learn more... EDITABLE CLOUD PC ALERT RULE CONDITIONS What is the feature? The conditions section of an Intune alert rule can now be edited directly in Nerdio Manager, the same way Cloud PC alert conditions already could, and the same way it works in the Intune portal. What does it do for me? You no longer need to make this kind of change in the Intune admin center and wait for it to sync back: though be aware that changes here update the underlying Intune alert rule itself, so they affect every tool that reads that rule, not only Nerdio Manager. How do I configure and use it? Open the alert condition and select Edit . Change the Conditions , Severity , Notifications , Native intune alerts , and Portal pop-up settings as needed. Select OK . Further reading: Alerts and notifications

items.title: Template-based configuration policies:
items.summary: Nerdio Manager now supports Windows configuration policies based on Intune templates . This is in addition to Settings catalog policies, which are available via Policy Studio . These policies can be created, viewed, and edited, with a template selector that limits the available settings categories to those the chosen template supports. Learn more... WINDOWS CONFIGURATION POLICIES BASED ON INTUNE TEMPLATES What is the feature? The Intune policy editor now supports Windows configuration policies based on Intune templates. What does it do for me? If you prefer working from Microsoft's own Intune templates rather than building a Settings catalog policy from scratch, you now have that option inside Nerdio Manager. How do I configure and use it? Navigate to Endpoints › Intune > Policy Management , and select the Configuration Profiles tab. Select New . In the profile type dropdown, select Configuration . From the template dropdown, select Intune Templates , then an available template. You can then configure and assign the policy as normal. Further reading: Intune policies and configurations

items.title: Script backup comparison readability:
items.summary: The script backup comparison view now highlights changes in the Base info and Assignments sections using the same editor and color treatment as the script content comparison, replacing the greyed-out text that made differences easy to miss.

items.title: Superseded apps and device compliance:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where a required Intune application that had been superseded was treated as missing, leaving the session host in drain mode and outside auto-scale indefinitely. Superseded applications are now excluded from managed application compliance evaluation.

items.title: Policy Studio assignments panel:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the Policy Studio assignments panel did not scroll, making assignments unreachable and policy settings inaccessible on policies carrying a large number of assignments. The panel can now be resized and scrolled, and its state persists between visits.

items.title: Rotate LAPS password permissions:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the Rotate local admin password action could fail in tenants that do not have Intune privileged operations enabled, following a Microsoft change to the Graph permission required by the rotate action.

items.title: Bulk conditional access policy actions:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the Confirm button stayed disabled when applying the Policy action selected bulk action to Conditional Access policies whose current states differed. Policies already in the selected state are now skipped rather than blocking the action.

items.title: Control over failed application update behavior:
items.summary: A new option on the Install WinGet application action, available at both deployment policy and application group level, prevents Nerdio Manager from uninstalling and reinstalling an application when an upgrade fails. When enabled, the action is marked as failed and the existing installation is left in place. Learn more... CONTROL OVER UNINSTALLATION BEHAVIOR AFTER FAILED APPLICATION UPGRADE What is the feature? A new "Do not uninstall if upgrade fails" option on the Install WinGet application action, available at both deployment policy and application group level. What does it do for me? Prevents Nerdio Manager from uninstalling and reinstalling an application when an upgrade fails: the failed action is simply marked as failed, and the existing installation is left in place, so users aren't left without the application at all. How do I configure and use it? Select the option when configuring the applications list on a deployment policy or application group. Further reading: UAM: Manage deployment policies UAM: Manage applications

items.title: Shell App detection before unzipping:
items.summary: For Zipped files, a new option allows a Shell App detection script to run before its package is downloaded and unzipped, avoiding the delay of extracting large archives where detection alone can determine the outcome. This option may also be used with multi-version Shell Apps, provided Detect before unzipping is enabled. Learn more... DETECT SHELL APPLICATION VERSION BEFORE UNZIPPING What is the feature? Shell apps gain a Detect version before unzipping option, which runs the detection script before a zipped package is downloaded and unzipped rather than after, and this can now be combined with multi-version shell apps, a combination that wasn't previously supported. What does it do for me? Avoids the delay of extracting large archives in cases where detection alone can determine the outcome, which previously required downloading and unzipping every candidate version to identify the right one. How do I configure and use it? Enable the option on the shell app's version settings, alongside the existing Unzip option. Further reading: UAM: Manage shell apps

items.title: Intune application assignments in properties:
items.summary: The Intune application properties dialog now shows assignments, listing the assignment type (Required, Available for enrolled devices, or Uninstall), whether each group is included or excluded, and the group name.

items.title: Intune application property editing:
items.summary: Building on the ability to view native Intune application properties introduced in 8.1, admins can now edit those properties through a new wizard. Learn more... EDIT NATIVE INTUNE APPLICATION PROPERTIES What is the feature? Building on the ability to view native Intune application properties, admins can now edit those properties directly through a dedicated wizard (General, Ownership, Links, Program tabs), and the application's Properties view now also shows its assignments. What does it do for me? You can make small corrections to an Intune-sourced application's install/uninstall commands, links, or ownership without needing to go back to the Intune admin center, and see at a glance who an application is assigned to and how. How do I configure and use it? From the application's action menu in the catalog, select Edit to change properties, or Properties to view them (including assignments). Further reading: UAM: Manage applications

items.title: Available assignment mode for Intune apps:
items.summary: Applications deployed through Intune can now be assigned as Available, publishing them to Company Portal for users to install themselves, in addition to the existing Required behavior. The selector is offered on deployment policies, application groups, and the REST API; Required remains the default, and Available applies to Win32 applications only. Learn more... ASSIGN INTUNE APPLICATIONS AS AVAILABLE FOR USER INSTALL What is the feature? Applications deployed through Intune can now be assigned as Available, publishing them to Company Portal for users to install themselves, in addition to the existing Required behavior. What does it do for me? Gives you the same optional-install flexibility Intune itself offers, for applications you deploy through Nerdio Manager, rather than only mandatory installs. How do I configure and use it? Choose Required or Available from the Assignment type field on the deployment policy or application group. Available applies to Win32 applications only, and Required remains the default. Further reading: UAM: Manage applications

items.title: Shell App and Scripted Sequence cache cleanup:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where Shell App and Scripted Sequence deployments did not clear their local cache after completing, causing storage use to grow over time. Temporary folders are now created in a dedicated location and removed after 24 hours.

items.title: Application install job serialization failure:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where an application install job could fail with a serialization error when no applications were returned by the configured WinGet sources.

items.title: Large-scale sequence execution:
items.summary: The Scripted Sequences feature has been reworked to run a single sequence across substantially larger Intune device populations (up to 1000 per execution) without devices being dropped. This limit is planned for removal when the feature moves to general availability. Learn more... RUN SCRIPTED SEQUENCES ON UP TO 1000 INTUNE DEVICES PER EXECUTION What is the feature? Scripted Sequences can now run a single sequence across up to 1,000 Intune devices per execution without devices being dropped, and Scripted Sequences plus Task Worker Analytics now have their own dedicated RBAC scopes under an Automation section. What does it do for me? You can comfortably use Scripted Sequences at production scale rather than only in smaller pilots, and you can grant scoped access to run or audit sequences without handing out the full Admin role. How do I configure and use it? The 1,000-device limit applies automatically: no configuration needed. For RBAC, see the configuration guidance in Role-based access control (RBAC): Custom roles to assign the Automation > Scripted Sequences and/or Task Worker Analytics scopes (Read Only or Manage) on a custom role. Further reading: Run and audit Scripted Sequences Role-based access control (RBAC): Custom roles

items.title: RBAC support for Scripted Sequences:
items.summary: Scripted sequences and their executions now have dedicated RBAC scopes under a new Automation section, each offering Read Only and Manage access. Read Only covers visibility of sequences, executions, and their related tasks, while Manage adds add, edit, clone, delete, run, force run, and cancel; the Scripted Actions selector has also moved under Automation.

items.title: RBAC support for Task Worker Analytics:
items.summary: Task Worker Analytics pages now have their own RBAC scope under the Automation section, with Read Only and Manage access levels, completing RBAC coverage across the Scripted Sequences feature set.

items.title: Breakdown of Other costs in User Cost Attribution:
items.summary: The Other costs value on the User Cost Attribution page is now a link that opens a full per-service breakdown, previously available only through the Power BI connector. Learn more... "OTHER COSTS" BREAKDOWN FOR USER COST ATTRIBUTION What is the feature? The Other costs value on the User Cost Attribution page is now a link that opens a full per-service breakdown. What does it do for me? You no longer need the Power BI connector to see what's actually inside your "Other" cost bucket (App Service, Key Vault, SQL DB, and similar shared resources): it's one click away in the portal. How do I configure and use it? Select the Other value on the User Cost Attribution page. Further reading: User cost attribution analytics

items.title: Per-usage-type Real-Time Insights thresholds:
items.summary: Real-Time Insights thresholds can now be set independently for AVD personal, AVD pooled, and Windows 365 endpoints.

items.title: Per-endpoint Real-Time Insights polling:
items.summary: Admins can now raise the polling interval for an individual AVD, Windows 365, or Intune-connected endpoint for a limited period when troubleshooting, after which it returns to the default. The interval in use is shown on both the overview and the endpoint page. Learn more... PER-ENDPOINT POLLING INTERVAL CONFIGURATION FOR REAL-TIME INSIGHTS What is the feature? You can temporarily raise the polling interval for a single AVD, Windows 365, or Intune-connected endpoint while troubleshooting; it reverts to the normal cadence automatically. What does it do for me? Lets you get faster data from one specific device you're actively investigating, without changing the polling cadence for your whole environment. How do I configure and use it? Go to the endpoint's Endpoint Diagnostics page, and select the Polling Interval tab. Choose a faster polling interval. Set how long it should apply, from 15 minutes to 24 hours. Further reading: Insights: Real-Time

items.title: Polling intervals per endpoint type:
items.summary: Real-Time Insights polling intervals can now be set independently for AVD, Windows 365, and Intune-connected devices.

items.title: Azure Local on the Health page:
items.summary: The Health page now includes an Azure Local section reporting connection status, alerts, updates, and security status, shown only where Azure Local is in use. Each tile reflects the worst status across all linked clusters. Learn more... HEALTH INSIGHTS FOR AZURE LOCAL What is the feature? Health Insights adds an Azure Local section where Azure Local is in use; Subnet IP Usage moves here from the AVD area of Insights; and App Service/database charts can now be filtered to a specific instance, with status-table entries linking through to the relevant section. What does it do for me? One health page now covers hybrid infrastructure alongside Azure-native resources, and it's easier to drill into a specific App Service plan or database rather than seeing an aggregate view only. How do I configure and use it? No configuration needed: these sections and filters appear automatically on the existing Health page where relevant. Further reading: Insights: Health

items.title: Real-Time Insights Global Pools support:
items.summary: Real-Time Insights deployment options now include the ability to deploy to Nerdio Global Pools.

items.title: Health page layout updates:
items.summary: Subnet IP Usage has moved from AVD to the Health page, and App Service and database charts can now be filtered to a specific instance, labeled with the integration that uses it. Entries in the status table now link through to the relevant section of Insights.

items.title: Executive Insights reporting lower-than-expected Projected Native Costs and Nerdio Manager Savings:
items.summary: Resolved an issue that could result in Estimated Native Costs (AVD) being understated, also resulting in Estimated Nerdio ROI (AVD) being lower than expected. Learn more... ROI ESTIMATION ADJUSTMENTS What has changed? Three Executive Insights dashlets are renamed to make their AVD-only scope explicit - Actual Cost (AVD) , Estimated Savings (AVD) , and Estimated Nerdio ROI (AVD) - and now exclude Nerdio Manager's own resource costs from their calculations. The $10-per-MAU licensing-cost fallback is removed in favor of an error if the Azure Cost Management API can't supply real licensing cost data, and a message now appears encouraging greater use of auto-scale where ROI is very low or negative. How does the change benefit me? More accurate, better-scoped cost and ROI figures, and a clearer explanation when the numbers can't be trusted (rather than a silent, possibly-misleading fallback estimate). How do I configure and use it? No configuration needed: these are calculation and display changes to the existing Insights: Executive dashlets. Further reading: Insights: Executive V8.2 changes to Executive Insights: AVD-Focused Reporting and ROI Changes

items.title: Max hourly rate in Modeler limited to 999:
items.summary: Max hourly rate has been increased to 99,999 to support broader set of currencies.

items.title: Unable to export more than 25 rows with Intune Insights:
items.summary: Export will now include all rows within the current query.

items.title: Multiple REST API credentials:
items.summary: Admins can now create, view, and revoke multiple REST API client secrets from the REST API settings, each with a name and an expiration date defaulting to one year, so one integration's credential can be rotated without disrupting the others. Existing secrets continue to work and appear in the list. Learn more... MULTIPLE REST API CREDENTIALS What is the feature? Admins can create, view, and revoke multiple REST API client secrets, each with its own name and expiration date (defaulting to one year). What does it do for me? One integration's credential can be rotated without disrupting any others sharing the same REST API app registration: previously, all integrations shared one secret. How do I configure and use it? Navigate to System > Settings > Environment > Integrations > REST API . Select Create API Key , and give it a name and expiration date. Copy the generated Value immediately: it's shown only once. Existing keys continue to work and appear in the same table. Further reading: REST API Getting Started with REST API Integration

items.title: Entra ID PIM support for Nerdio Manager roles:
items.summary: Nerdio Manager roles can now be assigned through PIM-enabled Entra ID groups, with an option to require PIM-backed groups for selected roles and an in-product page for admins to activate their membership with a justification and duration. Cumulative RBAC must be enabled. The following Microsoft Graph permissions are required: PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.Read.AzureADGroup (Application) PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.Read.AzureADGroup (Application) RoleManagementPolicy.Read.AzureADGroup (Application) PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup (Delegated) Learn more... NERDIO MANAGER ROLE ASSIGNMENT THROUGH PIM-ENABLED ENTRA GROUPS What is the feature? Nerdio Manager roles can be assigned through PIM-enabled Entra ID groups, with an option to require PIM-backed groups for selected roles, and an in-product page for admins to activate their membership with a justification and duration. What does it do for me? Brings just-in-time, approval-gated privileged access to Nerdio Manager roles, matching how you may already handle privileged Azure/Entra roles elsewhere. How do I configure and use it? Cumulative RBAC must be enabled first. Navigate to System > Settings > Environment > Integrations > PIM for Groups , and select Configure . Enable Use PIM for Groups and grant the requested Microsoft Graph permissions when prompted. Admins then activate eligible roles from the My Privileged Access page, with a justification and duration.

items.title: Private Endpoints settings page:
items.summary: A new Private Endpoints page under System > Settings > Nerdio shows the current private endpoint and DNS configuration, is read-only in this release. Learn more... PRIVATE ENDPOINT SETTINGS PAGE What is the feature? A new, read-only Private Endpoints page shows the private endpoint and DNS configuration Nerdio Manager uses to reach its Azure back-end resources. What does it do for me? Gives you visibility into private endpoint and DNS health for Nerdio Manager's own infrastructure (automation accounts, Key Vault, SQL Server, storage account, and web app) in one place, without having to check each resource in Azure individually. How do I configure and use it? Navigate to System > Settings > Environment > Nerdio tab > Private Endpoints . Review the Resource, DNS Name, Private DNS Zone, Private IP, Public Access, and Private Endpoints columns, or select Refresh or Export CSV . It's read-only in this release.

items.title: Additional logs in Request Logs:
items.summary: The Request Logs action on a failed task now collects a broader default set of logs and allows admins to include additional locations, reducing the need to retrieve logs manually from the affected host.

items.title: UPN and profile photo in the account menu:
items.summary: The account menu now shows the signed-in user's UPN, and the header avatar displays their profile photo where one is available, falling back to the default icon.

items.title: In-product installation registration:
items.summary: Registering an installation is now completed within Nerdio Manager rather than redirecting to an external page, with the CAPTCHA check shown in a modal during initial setup.

items.title: PowerShell 7.4 runbook support:
items.summary: Runbooks can now run in PowerShell 7.4, using runtime environments and direct API calls in place of the older SDK, enabled by an opt-in setting.

items.title: Nerdio Terraform provider (Public Preview):
items.summary: A Nerdio-owned Terraform provider now allows AVD resources to be managed as code, covering host pool creation and deletion, user assignment, session host creation and deletion, and host pool settings. The Terraform provider can be accessed at https://github.com/Get-Nerdio/NME-Terraform-Provider . Learn more... NERDIO TERRAFORM PROVIDER What is the feature? A new Nerdio Terraform provider supports managing AVD resources as code: host pool creation and deletion, user assignment, session host creation and deletion, and host pool settings. What does it do for me? Lets you manage AVD resources through your existing Terraform/infrastructure-as-code workflows rather than only through the Nerdio Manager UI or REST API.

items.title: Self-Service moved to its own navigation section:
items.summary: The end-user self-service page has moved out of Cloud Desktops > Azure Virtual Desktop into its own Self-Service section under Cloud Desktops, positioned after Migrate, where it now appears as Portal. The page itself, its data, and its behavior are unchanged.

items.title: Consistent Cloud PC removal during migration:
items.summary: Cloud PC to AVD migration now uses the same removal experience and background process as the Remove host action on the Hosts page.

items.title: Update runbook modernized:
items.summary: The update runbook now uses native Az PowerShell commands for App Service deployment and App Service/WebJob management, in place of direct Kudu REST calls.

items.title: REST API enhancements:
items.summary: Several areas of NME can now be managed programmatically through the REST API: RDP profiles: Host pool RDP profiles can be listed, retrieved, created, updated, and deleted. VM profiles: Host pool VM deployment profiles can be listed, retrieved, created, updated, and deleted. Linked resources: Capacity reservation groups, dedicated host groups, proximity placement groups, and signing certificates can be listed, linked, and unlinked. Intune alert conditions: Intune alert conditions can be managed, including the severity set against each condition. Cloud PC alert conditions: Cloud PC alert conditions can be managed, including activation, severity, notification and portal pop-up settings, native Intune alerts, and email recipients. Entra ID tenant linking: Additional Entra ID tenants can be linked and unlinked using an existing app registration, with support for the Azure Global, US Government, and China clouds.

items.title: Bulk migration from Windows 365 Enterprise to AVD Personal:
items.summary: Multiple Cloud PCs can now be migrated in a single operation. Shared parameters are configured once and applied to every selected device, with per-device status on the Migrations page and individual failures no longer canceling the batch.

items.title: Breadcrumbs aligned to the new navigation menu:
items.summary: Breadcrumbs across all pages now reflect their nesting level in the new navigation menu.

items.title: Group membership permissions checked during Cloud PC to AVD migration:
items.summary: Migration with Cloud PC removal is not permitted when the admin does not have modify permissions on the assigned groups.

items.title: AVD Agent and FSLogix versions missing from Updates page:
items.summary: We have re-added these version numbers to our Update page based on customer feedback.

items.title: Duplicate Console Connect platform scripts in Intune:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where Nerdio Manager could create duplicate Intune platform scripts instead of reusing the existing one, leaving stale Console Connect scripts and groups behind. Script retrieval now retries before creating a new script, with improved logging.

items.title: Subscription linking error with managed identity:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where linking an additional Azure subscription using an existing user-assigned managed identity could fail with an "Object reference not set to an instance of an object" error and create no task. Subscriptions can now be linked with a shared managed identity as expected.

items.title: Data Protection keys migration script error:
items.summary: Resolved an issue in the Data Protection keys migration script where a missing Key Vault key would cause the script to terminate before completing. The script now handles a non-existent key correctly and runs without error.

items.title: Console Connect blackened screen showing service account:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where using the Blacken Screen option in Console Connect displayed the Nerdio service account to the end user instead of the technician's account.

items.title: RBAC script using retired PowerShell modules:
items.summary: Resolved an issue where the RBAC role activation script (enable_roles.ps1) failed because it relied on the retired AzureAD PowerShell modules and blocked AAD Graph API. The script now uses Microsoft Graph, supports local PowerShell and Azure Cloud Shell execution, and migrates existing role assignments and owners without duplication.

items.title: Device name template (AVD to Windows 365 migration):
items.summary: When migrating an AVD Personal host to Windows 365 Enterprise, the "Device name template" field in the migration wizard does not apply to the provisioned Cloud PC. It retains the original AVD session host name instead. We're working to determine the root cause; this field will be removed from the migration wizard in a future release until issue is resolved.

items.title: Azure Virtual Desktop:
items.summary: Azure Files management with 'Smart' access tier storage accounts: Resolved an issue where Azure Files management would fail with an "Unknown StorageAccountAccessTier value" error when a storage account using the Blob Storage 'Smart' access tier existed.

items.title: Platform:
items.summary: Configurable maximum VM limit for legacy VDI to AVD Personal and Windows 365 Enterprise migrations: The maximum number of VMs permitted in a legacy VDI to AVD Personal or Windows 365 Enterprise migration is now configurable via the App Service setting Features:VdiMigration:UnmanagedVmToAny:MaxVms (default: 50), raised from the previous fixed maximum of 20. Note Nerdio recommends that customers raise this limit incrementally in batches of 50 (50, 100, 150, etc.) to ensure that migration success rate for their environment remains consistent as this value is increased.

items.title: AVD Personal to Windows 365 Flex Dedicated migration:
items.summary: Single and bulk migration support from AVD Personal to Windows 365 Flex Dedicated is now available in Public Preview!

items.title: Offline install support for Terraform:
items.summary: Added an optional app_package_local_path variable to the NME Terraform installer, allowing customers with disconnected or restricted IaC environments to point to a local zip package.

items.title: Windows 365 Flex Dedicated:
items.summary: The migration wizard now supports Windows 365 Flex Dedicated as a destination, alongside Windows 365 Enterprise.

items.title: Observability & AI:
items.summary: Real-Time Insights errors for non-onboarded hosts: Resolved an issue where Real-Time Insights displayed errors referencing hosts not included in the RTI configuration, caused by duplicate values returned from an Azure Resource Graph request during the load devices step. UCA reports fail to build: Resolved a validation issue in User Cost Attribution that caused reports to be incorrectly reported as failed builds.

items.title: Introducing Global Pools for AVD [Preview]:
items.summary: Global Pools brings enhanced scalability, user distribution, failover, and management capabilities for large-scale AVD deployments. Global Pools is a Premium-only feature. With this release, the following are supported: Create new host pools as part of a Global Pool (only multi-session desktop/RemoteApp experiences are supported with this initial release) Group host pools into Pool Groups Configure Auto-scale and Scripted Actions for host pools that are part of a Global Pool Create an Assignment Policy to automatically assign or re-assign users to specific Pool Groups, based on Entra group membership Create a Failover Policy to reassign users to a different Pool Group (manual trigger) User assignment page to view which host pool and Pool Group a specific user is assigned to For more information, see the Global Pools overview . Additional documentation is coming soon.

items.title: Migrate:
items.summary: AVD Personal to Windows 365 Enterprise migration is now GA.

items.title: New navigation menu enabled by default:
items.summary: The redesigned left navigation menu, introduced as an opt-in toggle in 8.0, is now enabled by default for all users. Also introduced is a Favorites menu item — users can select their favorite pages using the star icons on the All Features page. The legacy menu will be retired with Nerdio Manager 8.2.

items.title: AVD Hybrid for Nutanix (Preview):
items.summary: Console Connect support: Console Connect is now supported. Auto-scale support: Auto-scale features are now available.

items.title: Session Time Limits profile:
items.summary: Session Time Limit settings are now configurable as a host pool profile.

items.title: Auto-revert option to Azure Capacity Extender:
items.summary: When enabled, stopped session hosts that were resized to an alternative SKU are automatically reverted to the host pool's default VM size when auto-scaling, ensuring configuration consistency and simplifying capacity management. The option is off by default.

items.title: Azure Files > User Profiles tab:
items.summary: Added a new dedicated page that displays details for all FSLogix user profiles, including assigned user, file name, file share, last logon time, size, quota, usage, and health. Users with multiple profiles across different file shares are also supported.

items.title: Azure Files v2 support:
items.summary: Nerdio Manager now supports the creation of Azure Files v2 storage accounts. Auto-scale support will be included in a future release.

items.title: Auto-scale host pool sizing percentage:
items.summary: When configuring auto-scale host pool sizing, you now have the option to configure the sizing as percentages, in addition to absolute counts.

items.title: Desktop Image selector for Cloud PC-certified images:
items.summary: Cloud PC-certified images will now always appear when creating or updating desktop images.

items.title: Auto-scale Analytics for Azure Local:
items.summary: Auto-scale Analytics now supports Azure Local host pools and can make recommendations around provisioning loads.

items.title: User Experience Sync (UES) management:
items.summary: Admins can now configure and manage Windows 365 User Experience Sync directly in Nerdio Manager, including enabling or disabling sync, selecting storage size, reviewing which users and devices are covered by a provisioning policy, and deleting profiles.

items.title: Settings surface restructure:
items.summary: The Windows 365 User Settings tab has been renamed to Settings and restructured to align with Microsoft's Cloud PC settings taxonomy, introducing a Settings Type selector when creating new objects to support additional setting types in future releases.

items.title: AI-Enabled Cloud PC configuration:
items.summary: Admins can now create and manage Cloud PC configurations directly in NME under Windows 365 > Settings , including enabling AI-enabled features for targeted user groups with inline Microsoft requirements guidance and Frontier enrollment validation.

items.title: AI Status Column: The All Devices grid now includes an AI Status column for Windows 365 Cloud PCs, showing the per-device AI-enabled state across three statuses (Enabled, Disabled, and N/A), with filterable and sortable views to identify at scale where AI features are applied or blocked
items.summary: AI Status Column: The All Devices grid now includes an AI Status column for Windows 365 Cloud PCs, showing the per-device AI-enabled state across three statuses (Enabled, Disabled, and N/A), with filterable and sortable views to identify at scale where AI features are applied or blocked.

items.title: Windows 365 Frontline renamed to Windows 365 Flex:
items.summary: Reflects Microsoft's rename of the Windows 365 Frontline license and product to Windows 365 Flex.

items.title: Policy Studio (Preview):
items.summary: Nested Policy Settings: Nested setting values may now be directly edited for supported policy types from the Settings Explorer tab, simplifying policy management. Nested Policy Results: The Policy Results page now supports viewing nested values for settings, providing greater visibility into policy details.

items.title: Change Approvals (Preview):
items.summary: Scheduled approvals: Change requestors can now set a scheduled execution time at request creation, rather than waiting until after approval. Approvers see the scheduled time before acting, and both approvers and requestors can reject or cancel before execution. This is not supported for Intune User Operating Mode . Lifecycle management: Pending requests now auto-cancel after a configurable inactivity period. Disabling approvals converts all pending requests to Cancelled while retaining history for a minimum of three years. Failed status: Introduced a new Failed status for requests where real-time execution was unsuccessful or a scheduled request exhausted three retry attempts, with a visual indicator and options to Execute now , Schedule , Cancel , or Reject . Auto-cancel on feature disable: Pending and approved requests are automatically cancelled when Intune integration, Policy Approvals, or User Mode settings conflict with their execution.

items.title: Enhanced Intune logging:
items.summary: Intune-related actions are now logged as a separate task within Nerdio Manager's job details, making it easier to review what happened during Intune-specific processing.

items.title: Configurable Retry Limits:
items.summary: Admins managing large environments can now increase the default Graph API retry count via separate app service settings for web (Feature:HttpOption:MaxRetries:Graph:Web, up to 5) and background (Feature:HttpOption:MaxRetries:Graph:Background, up to 6) services, reducing throttling failures at scale.

items.title: View Intune application properties:
items.summary: Admins can now view native Intune application properties directly from the application dropdown in the UAM catalog.

items.title: CSV export support:
items.summary: Added the ability to export the following to CSV: Deployment policy targets (pool, group, workspace) Deployment policy applications Shell Apps Unified Catalog (app repository, name, type, publisher, version, and favorite status)

items.title: AD Service Account Support:
